title: fix(telegram): typing held back by a flood wait is logged as an error
body:
Closes #191686

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the gateway logs an ERROR for every typing action that Telegram flood control held back, although the request was never sent.

## User Impact

User impact: during a Telegram flood wait, typing and preview updates that OpenClaw deliberately skips no longer write `telegram sendChatAction failed: ... (flood wait active; request not sent)` at ERROR. A 429 that Telegram itself returns, a final reply the limiter could not send within its delivery budget, and any other API failure still log at ERROR. The flood wait is still logged once at WARN by `telegram/flood`. Nothing about sending changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The account limiter answers a request it holds back with a synthetic 429, and grammY turns that into a `GrammyError`; `withTelegramApiErrorLogging` logged it like any API failure. The limiter now says which kind of hold-back it was:
- a replaceable update it skipped on purpose (typing or a preview during a flood wait, or a preview yielding to a pending reply) ends in `; replaceable update not sent)`;
- anything else it could not send (a final over the five-minute delivery budget, a non-replaceable request held at the network edge) keeps main's `; request not sent)`.

The logging owner skips only the first kind, for every operation it wraps, so the three typing call sites need no per-site filter, and the suffix has one definition, exported from `api-logging.ts` and used by the limiter. The error is still thrown, so typing keepalive failure counting and the chat-action cooldown behave as before.

The first revision of this PR matched `; request not sent)` and so also dropped the ERROR for a final over the delivery budget (ClawSweeper and Copilot, both correct). Fixed in `7ce6881989a`.

Simplification against an earlier draft of this branch: the first version exported a predicate from the limiter and added a `shouldLog` filter at each of the three typing call sites. This version keeps the decision in the logging wrapper.

## Evidence

- Regression test (`api-logging.test.ts`), one case per typing call site (inbound reply, recovered forum topic, outbound `sendTypingTelegram`), through grammY's `Api`, the real account throttler and chat-action handler, and a scripted Bot API:
  - Telegram 429s a preview edit, then typing during the wait is skipped.
  - After the wait, Telegram 429s typing itself, then returns a 400.
  - The test asserts that the `telegram/api` error logger receives exactly the real 429 and the 400, and that only 2 sendChatAction requests reached the network.
- Terminal case (`api-logging.test.ts`): Telegram floods a preview edit for 600 s, then a final `sendMessage` exceeds the delivery budget. The logger receives `telegram sendMessage failed: Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (429: Too Many Requests: retry after 600 (flood wait exceeds delivery budget; request not sent))`, and the final never reaches the network.
- `account-throttler.test.ts`: typing skipped at the gate and typing skipped at the network edge after the per-chat action queue both end in `(flood wait active; replaceable update not sent)`; Telegram's own 429 does not.
- Fail without, pass with:
  - With main's logger (no suppression), 3 of 14 `api-logging.test.ts` cases fail, each with the extra line `telegram sendChatAction failed: ...` (`telegram typing failed: ...` for the outbound case).
  - With the first revision's predicate (`c8eb2c05b6e`), the terminal case fails: the final's ERROR is missing.
  - With this head, both files pass: 38 of 38.
- Consumers: the 17 Telegram test files that import the limiter or the logging wrapper, or exercise flood waits and chat actions, pass (421 tests). `withTelegramApiErrorLogging` has 20 call sites in the extension; no test elsewhere asserts the skipped-update text.
- oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files, and the line-cap, assertion-safety and test-line ratchets pass against `586f5766569`. Test-line growth is 172 lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/telegram-typing-flood-log-level.txt` (170 at `7ce6881989a`; `8fec891ad7e` adds 2), and test-lines passes against main `cada32bb050`, which is back under its ceiling (slack 4). `8fec891ad7e` awaits the throttler release in the over-budget final test: CI's `check-test-types` (run 41697320147) failed with TS2322 at `api-logging.test.ts:207`, because the test returned `releaseAccountThrottler`'s `Promise<boolean>` from `onTestFinished`, which takes `Awaitable<void>`. The extensions test tsgo leaf reproduced it on `7ce6881989a` alone and merged with `cada32bb050`, passes on `cada32bb050` alone, and exits 0 on `8fec891ad7e`; `api-logging` and `account-throttler` pass 38/38.
- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `account-throttler.test.ts` 6.0 s and 5.7 s wall, 4.2 s and 4.2 s of tests; `api-logging.test.ts` 28.7 s (cold worker cache, 20.9 s of it compiling) and 7.9 s wall, 92 ms and 73 ms of tests. CI run 42047653236, Bun: `account-throttler.test.ts` 4.3 s of tests in a shared run (`checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-3`); `api-logging.test.ts` 218 ms of tests in a shared run (`checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-3`).

### Telegram Test Server E2E (exact head `77d841edb64a`, this branch merged with main after #190006)

Real Gateway built from this head and from `main` `8ebe740925ca`, a Telegram Test Server DM driven by a userbot, a scripted model streaming a long answer for about 30 s, `streaming.mode: "partial"`. The test proxy answers the first preview `editMessageText` with 429 `retry_after: 15`, so typing renewals fall inside the flood wait.

| | `main` 8ebe740925ca | this PR 77d841edb64a |
|---|---|---|
| ERROR `telegram sendChatAction failed: ... (flood wait active; request not sent))` | 4 | 0 |
| `telegram/flood` WARN for the wait | 1 | 1 |
| Typing seen in the chat | gap during the wait | gap during the wait (held back as before) |
| Final answer | complete (end marker present) | complete (end marker present) |

- The other WARN lines differ only by host load (main-thread stall reports). The head run also logged one teardown-time ERROR, `reconnect delivery drain failed: Gateway is shutting down`, when the harness stopped the Gateway; it is unrelated to API logging.
- `account-throttler.ts` keeps main's elapsed-time delivery budget from #190006; only the skip classification is added.

### Gateway run (2026-11-09)

A real Gateway from a built `dist` (`node dist/index.js gateway run`, Node 26.12.1, macOS arm64; Vitest also on Node), a local fake Telegram Bot API that grammY talks to as its transport, and a scripted Responses provider. Base: main `3855c896edd`. Head: this PR merged onto that main (`git merge-tree --write-tree 3855c896edd 8fec891ad7e` = `772df62bc25`, no conflicts, same patch-id as this PR's diff). The fake API refuses in Telegram's shape: HTTP status equal to `error_code`, `ok: false`, `parameters.retry_after`. One DM, `streaming.mode: "partial"`, four turns:
1. Telegram 429s the first preview edit with `retry_after` 8. The answer keeps streaming for about 12 s, so typing renewals (every 4 s) land inside the wait.
2. Telegram 429s typing with `retry_after` 2.
3. Telegram returns 400 `Bad Request: chat not found` for typing.
4. Telegram 429s typing with `retry_after` 600, which puts the final reply over the delivery budget.

ERROR lines in the Gateway file log, 3 runs per build (2 at info, 1 at debug):

| ERROR line | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `telegram sendChatAction failed: ... (flood wait active; request not sent))`, typing held back during the 8 s wait | 2, 2, 1 | 0, 0, 0 |
| `telegram sendChatAction failed: ... (429: Too Many Requests: retry after 2)` and `retry after 600` | 2 each run | 2 each run |
| `telegram sendChatAction failed: ... (400: Bad Request: chat not found)` | 1 each run | 1 each run |
| `(flood wait exceeds delivery budget; request not sent))`: `sendMessage failed` x2, `final reply failed`, `fallback delivery failed` | 4 each run | 4 each run |

- How many typing renewals fall inside the 8 s wait depends on timing; it was 1 or 2 per run.
- No typing request reached the fake API during the wait, in any run on either build.
- At debug both builds log `telegram typing failed target=777` for each held-back request: main with `(flood wait active; request not sent)`, this PR with `(flood wait active; replaceable update not sent)`. The typing is still attempted and refused here; only the ERROR line is gone.
- The `telegram/flood` WARN fires once per flood on both builds, 3 per run.
- Telegram's own 429 on the preview edit logs only that WARN, on main and here.
- In turn 4 no `sendMessage` reached the network on either build.

Main at debug, the 8 s wait:

```
WARN  telegram/flood  Telegram flood control on editMessageText: all calls for this bot wait 8s; replaceable update skipped
ERROR telegram/api    telegram sendChatAction failed: Call to 'sendChatAction' failed! (429: Too Many Requests: retry after 8 (flood wait active; request not sent))
DEBUG                 telegram typing failed target=777: GrammyError: Call to 'sendChatAction' failed! (429: Too Many Requests: retry after 8 (flood wait active; request not sent))
```

This PR at debug, same window:

```
WARN  telegram/flood  Telegram flood control on editMessageText: all calls for this bot wait 8s; replaceable update skipped
DEBUG                 telegram typing failed target=777: GrammyError: Call to 'sendChatAction' failed! (429: Too Many Requests: retry after 7 (flood wait active; replaceable update not sent))
DEBUG                 telegram typing failed target=777: GrammyError: Call to 'sendChatAction' failed! (429: Too Many Requests: retry after 3 (flood wait active; replaceable update not sent))
```

- Not covered end to end: real Telegram flood control on a live bot. Crabline's Telegram server cannot return a flood 429 for a Bot API method, so the Gateway run above uses its own fake Bot API.
- Not shown by the Gateway run: a preview edit skipped during a wait. Answer deltas arrived inside the 8 s wait, but no edit reached the fake API and nothing logged one, so the run does not tell a skipped edit from one never tried; the unit tests cover it. Also not provoked: the "yielded to a pending reply" skip, and typing in a forum topic.
